bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Astrophysicist Salary in Australia

When searching for an astrophysicist salary in Australia, the most reliable sources are the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) and the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office. The ABS classifies astrophysicists under Physicists (including Astronomers) in its occupation data. According to Jobs and Skills Australia, 87% of physicists work full-time, averaging 41 hours per week, with a median age of 41 years. While the exact median weekly earnings for physicists are not publicly available in the latest search results, the ABS reports that professionals in Australia earn an average hourly total cash earnings of $64.50 per hour (May 2025). For a 38-hour week, this gives an annual gross salary of approximately $127,452. The on-site reference uses the more recent ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) of $2,083.70 per week for full-time adult ordinary time, which equates to $108,352 per year. Astrophysicists, as highly skilled professionals, typically earn above this national average.

## Hourly to Annual Conversion: The 38-Hour Week

The standard conversion for any hourly rate to annual pay is: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. We assume 38 hours per week, which is the full-time benchmark used by the Fair Work Ombudsman for the National Minimum Wage. For example, at $64.50 per hour, the calculation is $64.50 × 38 × 52 = $127,452. If you work 41 hours (the average for physicists), the annual figure would be higher, but we use 38 hours for consistency. The fortnightly equivalent is weekly pay × 2. For $127,452 annually, weekly pay is $2,451, so fortnightly is $4,902 before tax.

## National Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, giving $33.05 per hour including loading. However, astrophysicists are usually not covered by awards—most physicists are covered by individual arrangements or enterprise agreements. The ABS data shows that 38.5% of all employees have pay set by individual arrangement, while 34.6% have collective agreements. Award-only coverage is only 22.7%. For astrophysicist salary, the rate is typically negotiated, not set by an award. The [pay guides](/blog) on this site show minimum rates for various awards, but astrophysicists are generally above those minima.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a $127,452 annual salary, the super contribution is $15,294.40 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional payment. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more about salary sacrificing and contribution caps.

## Tax and Medicare

Resident tax rates for 2026–27 are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a $127,452 annual salary, the tax estimate (using the full tax-free threshold) is approximately $29,267 plus Medicare $2,549, leaving a take-home pay of $95,636 per year. The [take-home pay](/). The reader types a base hourly rate, and a checkbox adds 25% loading on top. Never type a rate that already includes loading. The calculator uses the 38-hour week and applies the assumptions above.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
